an5.7:1.1: “Bhikkhus, beings for the most part are captivated by sensual pleasures.
an5.7:1.2: When a clansman has forsaken the sickle and carrying-pole and gone forth from the household life into homelessness, he can be described as a clansman who has gone forth out of faith.
an5.7:1.4: Sensual pleasures, whether of this or that kind, can be obtained by a youth.
an5.7:1.5: Inferior sensual pleasures, middling sensual pleasures, and superior sensual pleasures are all reckoned simply as sensual pleasures.
an5.7:1.6: “Suppose a young infant boy, ignorant, lying on his back, were to put a stick or pebble in his mouth because of his nurse’s heedlessness.
an5.7:1.7: His nurse would quickly attend to him and try to take it out.
an5.7:1.9: If she could not quickly take it out, she would brace the boy’s head with her left hand and, hooking a finger of her right hand, she would take it out even if she had to draw blood.
an5.7:1.11: There would be some distress for the boy—
an5.7:1.13: but the nurse has to do so for his good and welfare, out of compassion for him.
an5.7:1.14: However, when the boy has grown up and has enough sense, the nurse would be unconcerned about him, thinking:
an5.7:1.15: ‘The boy can now look after himself. He won’t be heedless.’
an5.7:2.1: “So too, so long as a bhikkhu is still not accomplished in faith in cultivating wholesome qualities, in a sense of shame in cultivating wholesome qualities, in moral dread in cultivating wholesome qualities, in energy in cultivating wholesome qualities, and in wisdom in cultivating wholesome qualities, I must still look after him.
an5.7:2.2: But when that bhikkhu is accomplished in faith in cultivating wholesome qualities … accomplished in wisdom in cultivating wholesome qualities, then I am unconcerned about him, thinking:
an5.7:2.3: ‘The bhikkhu can now look after himself. He won’t be heedless.’”
